newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's warring parties gear up for talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's warring parties gear up for talks.

text.p: Zaire and its ailing and embattled president Mobutu Sese Seko will announce their team for talks with Laurent Kabila's rebels shortly, state radio said on Monday.

The radio reported fighting around the rebel-held port of Moba on Lake Tanganyika, suggesting the two sides were jockeying for position ahead of talks which could start in South Africa before the end of the week.

Earlier, expatriates in the southern mining capital of Lubumbashi said rebels had moved into the rail town of Kamina without a fight, effectively cutting off the copperbelt province of Shaba and hundreds of troops there from the rest of Zaire.
Meanwhile relief workers raced against time to move 20,000 exhausted Hutu refugees away from the rebel-held city of Kisangani before a rebel deadline expired later on Monday.

State radio gave no precise date for the start of negotiations but referred to "talk of a possible first meeting" in South Africa before the end of the week. Rebel spokesman in the east have said the talks could be as early as Thursday.

"There is talk of a possible first meeting between the representatives of the rebellion and those from Kinshasa towards the end of the week in South Africa," the radio said. "In Kinshasa we should know within the coming days the names of the personalities who will make up the committee of negotiators."
Rebels took up arms in October, vowing to topple Mobutu, who has dominated Zaire since seizing power in 1965.

Representatives from the two sides, brought together by African leaders at a special Organisation of African Unity summit in Togo last week, agreed to the principle of talks and a ceasefire -- without nailing down dates.

Mobutu has asked parliament to appoint a seven-member negotiating team representing government, the judiciary, the opposition, his own presidential movement and with a special representative from the presidency to take charge of the talks.
Professor Kabuya Lumuna, a Mobutu spokesman, said details of the team and the date and venue would be known shortly.
Rebel spokesmen say the talks will prepare for a meeting between Kabila and Mobutu to negotiate Mobutu's departure.
The revolt, which began while Mobutu was in Europe recuperating after surgery for prostate cancer, has weakened the veteran leader's grip on the sprawling Central African nation.
Impoverished ordinary Zaireans, hungry for change, openly welcome the arrival of Kabila and his forces.
Expatriates in Lubumbashi, Zaire's second largest city and a designated rebel target, said Kamina fell to the rebels early on Monday -- after the army there had melted away.
They said the rebels could use trains there to speed their advance on Lubumbashi to the south east.

A senior defence ministry official said earlier that fighting around Moba began on Friday. The same official said that communications with soldiers in the field had become difficult because the rainy season was in full swing.
State radio said the rebels were within 200 km (125 miles) of Lubumbashi but did not specify where.

The Tutsi-dominated rebels gave Rwandan and Burundian Hutus an extra day to move away from Zaire's third city Kisangani for security reasons. They say the Hutus might include armed hardliners blamed for the 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda.
